subject: Extension of the product safety scope and the safety documents to the brownfield RCC examples (0008a/0008b/0008c) and to the IWDG watchdog (0009a)
statements: Which target ASIL do you set for the IWDG (watchdog) product scope? -> "ASIL B"

For the RCC brownfield examples (0008a/b/c), the signed RCC SSA/TAA v1.0 match their inputs but were written for factory-generated code. How should they be extended? -> "Draft v1.1 to sign (Recommended)"
decision: IWDG: new scope decision SC-IWDG-2026-10-20 (example 0009a-iwdg-ll, target ASIL B set by the owner) in config/factory/safety-scope.yaml, with drafts SSA-IWDG-001 and TAA-IWDG-001 v0.1 registered UNSIGNED (basis bfee8b2ee260d6e114e2cf92b77336da4c8534e11efd53cf3c2a7995910b9286). RCC brownfield: drafts SSA-RCC-001 and TAA-RCC-001 v1.1 under config/factory/safety-documents/SC-RCC-2026-10-18/v1.1/, NOT registered; 0008a/0008b/0008c join SC-RCC-2026-10-18 only when the owner signs v1.1.
agent_note: All four documents were drafted by Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code) and carry the draft marker; nothing is signed. The basis hashes were computed as workorder.prepare does; 0002a, 0002b, 0008a, 0008b and 0008c share basis c62aa88c..., and the IWDG basis equals the inputs of run i003. The v1.1 drafts record the CAPA-051 finding: swe3_hal_author and swe4_test_author ran on DeepSeek before CAPA-051, and HAL r164 also ran its inspectors and Release Manager on DeepSeek.
